title: The teacher takes command
hookLine: Duryodhana asks his new commander for one thing: bring Yudhishthira to me alive
carry: acharya devo bhava: honor the teacher as god
tomorrow: Arjuna's far away. who can break Drona's wheel?

lines: TEACHER OF BOTH SETS OF COUSINS.
cards: A teacher takes command of an army sent against his own students.

Bhishma lies on the field, and the man the Kauravas choose to lead them is Drona, the master of arms who trained both sets of cousins as boys, who once tested the princes with a toy bird in a treetop and found that only Arjuna saw nothing but its head.
Duryodhana honors him, and Drona, pleased, offers him a gift: ask for whatever you want. Duryodhana's answer surprises him. Not Arjuna's death.
Not victory. Bring me Yudhishthira, he says. Alive.

teach.b: Drona is glad to hear it, at first. In Ganguli's telling, he praises Duryodhana: you don't want your cousin killed, so maybe you mean to make peace. But Duryodhana's reasons show.
A captured Yudhishthira could be drawn into the dice again, and the Pandavas sent back to the forest. Same game, second round. Drona agrees, with one condition: only if Arjuna isn't beside him.

So a band of Trigarta warriors swears an oath to challenge Arjuna and never come back until he's dead or they are: the samshaptakas, the sworn ones. Arjuna won't refuse a challenge, and he rides away.
Now step back, because this part of the story asks something hard. Hindus hold the teacher, the guru or acharya, almost as high as God.

teach.h: TREAT YOUR TEACHER AS A GOD
teach.b: The Taittiriya Upanishad tells a student leaving school: treat your mother as a god, your father as a god, your teacher as a god.
Acharya devo bhava. That's why, on the war's first morning, Yudhishthira walked unarmed to Drona, bowed to him and asked his blessing.
Drona gave it, and told him plainly that he was bound to the Kaurava side by what they had given him. So the epic holds both: the teacher is sacred, and a teacher can still stand on the wrong side.
Arjuna will honor Drona and fight him. In the coming days, that empty space where Arjuna should be will matter.

how: Hindus honor teachers on Guru Purnima, and many students touch a teacher's feet before a lesson, an exam or a performance; Drona is remembered as the guru of both the Kauravas and the Pandavas.

o: the teacher of both houses, now commanding the Kaurava army
the Trigarta warrior sworn to kill Arjuna or die trying
the dice master who plans to win Yudhishthira's kingdom

games.q: the new command — tap the pairs.
p: sworn to kill Arjuna or die
drawn away to answer their challenge

s: Duryodhana asked Drona to kill Yudhishthira
he asked for him alive, hoping to play the dice again.
Drona could take Yudhishthira only with Arjuna away
that was his own condition, said out loud.
in Hinduism a guru is just someone who teaches you a skill
the teacher is honored almost as God: acharya devo bhava. Yudhishthira bowed to Drona even across a battle line.

games.q: you're Yudhishthira on the war's first morning. your old teacher Drona is on the other side. what do you do?
o: walk over unarmed, bow, and ask his blessing.
avoid him; he chose the enemy.
send word you'll spare him if he switches sides.
games.why: Yudhishthira bows and asks his blessing, and Drona gives it, though he's bound to the Kaurava side. the guru is honored even across the battle line.

practice: Fold your hands at your chest. Many Hindu children learn a verse that begins Gurur Brahma, Gurur Vishnu: the teacher is Brahma, the teacher is Vishnu. Bring to mind one teacher who shaped you, in a classroom, a kitchen, a gym.
Breathing in, see their face. Breathing out, bow your head a little toward them, the way Yudhishthira bowed to Drona with armies watching. If you pray, thank God for them.
If you don't, simply thank them in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Drona. The teacher of the Kauravas and the Pandavas, now commanding the Kaurava army against his own students.

orig.note: the guru of both sets of cousins, and the Kaurava commander after Bhishma.

carryVoice: Your line: acharya devo bhava: honor the teacher as god. Even when the teacher rides against you. That's day eight hundred thirty-one.
